context:
Goal: every repo's main is protected the one shared way.
Problem (rule): the shared form requires one check, all-jobs-passed, but the script that sets protection accepts any number of --check names, so a session can set a form the rule does not allow.
Based on (read): docs/decisions/main-branch-protection.md:5 says main requires one check, all-jobs-passed.
Based on (read): skills/project-ops/scripts/protect.py:36 takes --check as a repeatable flag (main da8d8073).
Departs from: main, where protect.py accepts several required checks — it refuses more than one.

options.gain: No repo can be set up off the shared form by mistake.
options.how: protect.py stops with a message when given a second --check; the shared form stays one check.
options.label: Refuse more than one
options.lose: A repo that truly needs a second required check needs a code change and your word first.

options.how: protect.py keeps taking any number of --check names, as today.
options.label: Allow several
options.lose: A session can set protection the shared form does not allow, and nothing catches it.

title: Should the branch-protection script refuse more than one required check?
why: It makes the script match the single all-jobs-passed check the protection record requires.
